summary: Radar for 2026-10-19 (GLP-1 focus). Three things are new and accelerating. (1) Gray-market retatrutide has moved into mainstream safety news. The NY Post (Oct 16) and Futurism (Oct 17) reported the CBS finding that FDA received two death reports linked to products sold as retatrutide; FDA has not said whether either was verified. Stocktwits/MDLinx covered Lilly's six lawsuits, and NL Times (Oct 19) reported rising illegal use in the Netherlands. This is our proven retatrutide lane, and Lilly's Q3 call on Oct 29 is the next hook for a dated status update. (2) A 2-million-patient surgery study presented at ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 (Medical Xpress, Newswise, News-Medical, Medical Daily, Newsweek, Oct 18–19) linked GLP-1 use to 11% lower odds of major heart complications and 8% lower odds of infections after elective surgery. Our anesthesia Short did 83, so this is a strong 'Mounjaro or Ozempic before surgery?' rising topic. (3) SciTechDaily (Oct 19) is re-circulating retatrutide's first Phase 3 type 2 diabetes trial (TRANSCEND-T2D-1, 40 weeks). Different outlets quote different numbers (about 15% vs 17%), so the script must name the estimand. Steady performers stay on the list: tirzepatide vs semaglutide side effects (SURMOUNT-5), why results vary, stopping tirzepatide plus the Revita De Novo news, and compounded-product quality (Empower warning letter and recall, framed only as 'approved vs compounded, talk to your prescriber'). Long-form candidates are limited to next-gen decoders: retatrutide in type 2 diabetes, orforglipron's ACHIEVE-4 heart data (non-inferior vs insulin glargine, not superior), and CagriSema vs semaglutide. Lower-priority or caution items: NAION (scare topic, peaking), PCOS fertility (pregnancy label caveats), psoriasis and alcohol (early evidence). Rejected: price and switching content tied to telehealth or compounded sellers. Corrections from checking: the Zepbound KwikPen approval and the Wegovy subscription are early-2026 news being re-circulated, not new events.

candidates.topic: Is retatrutide approved yet? (Oct 2026): FDA received two death reports linked to products sold as retatrutide (CBS, unverified), Lilly's lawsuits against sellers, and the Dutch poisons centre's rising reports
candidates.angle: A calm 'what's confirmed?' Short. Retatrutide is not FDA- or EMA-approved as of Oct 2026, and Lilly's stated filing target is early 2027. FDA got two death reports (July and September) after people used products sold as retatrutide. A report is a warning sign, not proof of cause, and FDA hasn't said whether either was verified. Lilly says neither person was in a trial and calls the products black-market. The Netherlands poisons centre logged 6 retatrutide reports in 2025 and 12 in Jan–May 2026. Close with a prescriber line about approved options or clinical trials. Never name sellers and don't fear-bait.
candidates.why_now: The NY Post (Oct 16), Futurism (Oct 17) and NL Times (Oct 19) all ran gray-market retatrutide stories, and polskieradio/Philstar SEO pages show high search demand for 'retatrutide approval status' and 'FDA concerns retatrutide'. Our retatrutide Shorts median 98 views (1.75× typical), and the dated status question is our best Instagram format.

candidates.topic: Mounjaro or Ozempic before surgery: GLP-1 use linked to 11% lower odds of major heart complications and 8% lower odds of infections in more than 2 million adults having elective surgery (ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Taking a GLP-1 before surgery: safer or riskier?' Give the answer by 10 s. In this Epic Cosmos records study (US adults, elective surgery over 60 min, at least 24 h in hospital, 2016–2024), GLP-1 use was linked to 11% lower odds of heart attack, heart injury, stroke or death, and 8% lower odds of wound, urinary, lung or blood infections. It's observational and presented at a meeting, not peer-reviewed yet. The lead author says doctors still need more evidence. Practical message: always tell your surgeon and anesthesia team you're on a GLP-1 and follow their instructions. Never say 'stop before surgery'.
candidates.why_now: Coverage spread from Oct 18–19: Medical Xpress, Newswise, News-Medical, Inside Precision Medicine, Medical Daily, Newsweek and Becker's. The PubMed feed is also busy (knee, shoulder, spine, body contouring and aortic valve cohorts). Our anesthesia Short got 83 views, 1.5× the median.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide for type 2 diabetes: what the first Phase 3 trial (TRANSCEND-T2D-1, 40 weeks, vs placebo) found on weight and HbA1c
candidates.angle: Long-form decoder: 'Did retatrutide beat tirzepatide? What the first diabetes trial actually tested'. The answer is no head-to-head yet; this trial compared retatrutide with placebo. Lilly reported A1c falls of 1.7–2.0 points from a baseline of 7.9%. Weight loss is about 11.5–15.3% vs 2.6% on placebo in one estimand and up to 17% on the top dose in Lilly's efficacy estimand, so name the estimand every time. Include the 537 participants, the population (type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise) and that it's investigational as of Oct 2026. Bridge to the gray-market warning. A Short version can work as 'Retatrutide for diabetes: how much weight in 40 weeks?'.
candidates.why_now: SciTechDaily ran 'New triple-action drug helps people with diabetes lose up to 15%' on Oct 19, a fresh pop-science wave from older ADA data. Retatrutide search terms are among the strongest in today's feed, and next-gen decoders are our only long-form format that travels (median about 32 views).
